title: Edmonton Obesity Staging System (EOSS)
formula:
The EOSS stage is determined by the highest severity selection:

| Variable | Stage | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Obesity-related risk factors | None | 0 |
| Subclinical (examples include borderline HTN, impaired fasting glucose, etc.) | 1 | |
| Established (risk factors that require medical intervention, including HTN, DM type II, sleep apnea, etc.) | 2 | |
| Significant (risk factors that have led to end-organ damage, such as MI, HF, complications from DM, etc.) | 3 | |
| Severe (potentially end-stage obesity-related medical conditions) | 4 | |
| Physical symptoms or functional limitations | None | 0 |
| Mild (some dyspnea on exertion, occasional aches, fatigue, etc.) | 1 | |
| Moderate (some limitations in daily activity) | 2 | |
| Significant (unable to work or complete routine activities) | 3 | |
| Severe (disabling functional limitations) | 4 | |
| Psychological symptoms | None | 0 |
| Mild (symptoms of well-being impairment, without impact to quality of life) | 1 | |
| Moderate (depression, anxiety, eating disorders, quality of life is beginning to be impacted due to limitations) | 2 | |
| Significant (major depression, suicidal ideation, quality of life is significantly impacted) | 3 | |
| Severe (disabling psychological symptoms) | 4 | |

how_to_use.why:
- Helps identify patients at elevated risk of obesity-related complications, enabling prioritized and focused medical intervention.
- Can be used to guide, evaluate, and monitor the effectiveness and progress of obesity treatments.
how_to_use.when:
- Can be used in the outpatient setting as an alternative or adjunct to anthropometric measurements, such as BMI, waist circumference, or waist-to-hip ratio, in the assessment of obesity severity and associated health problems.
- May have utility in presurgical evaluations for predicting complications and mortality following bariatric surgery.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Traditional surrogate measures of body and visceral fat (e.g., BMI, WC) show significant interindividual variation, which can complicate the accurate estimation of morbidity and mortality risks.
- This tool evaluates obesity-related comorbidities, physical and functional impairments, and psychological factors to stage the health implications and clinical risks associated with increased body fat.
- Some components of this tool rely on clinical judgment, which can introduce variability in staging between different healthcare providers.
- The EOSS should be used in conjunction with other assessments and should not serve as the sole determinant of obesity-related health risks or treatment decisions.

next_steps.advice:
- This tool can be used to determine appropriate treatments and medical services for patients based on their individual obesity-related risks and complications.
- For patients undergoing bariatric surgery planning:

 - Stage 3 and 4 are associated with increased risk of postoperative complications, including a higher 30-day mortality.
 - Patients found to be in higher stages should be counseled on the increased risk of postoperative complications.
 - However, this tool should not be used to exclude patients from surgical consideration. The benefits of surgery often outweigh the risks and should be assessed by the clinician on a case-by-case basis.
next_steps.management:
The derivation study for this tool proposed management based on the resulting clinical and functional staging:

| Stage | Management |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Identify factors contributing to increased body weight. Provide counseling on lifestyle measures, such as healthy eating and physical activity. |
| 1 | Investigate for other (non-weight related) contributors to risk factors. Implement more intensive lifestyle interventions, including diet and exercise. Monitor risk factors and health status. |
| 2 | Initiate obesity treatments, including consideration for all behavioral, pharmacological, and surgical options. Closely monitor and manage comorbidities, as indicated. |
| 3 | Initiate more intensive obesity treatment. Aggressively manage comorbidities, as indicated. |
| 4 | Pursue aggressive obesity management, as deemed feasible. Consider additional measures, including pain management, occupational therapy, and psychosocial support. |

more_info:
Interpretation:

| Stage | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | No apparent obesity-related risk factors (e.g., blood pressure, serum lipids, fasting glucose, etc. within normal range). No physical symptoms. No psychopathology. No functional limitations and/or impairment of well being. |
| 1 | Presence of obesity-related subclinical risk factors (e.g., borderline hypertension, impaired fasting glucose, elevated liver enzymes, etc.). Mild physical symptoms (e.g., dyspnea on moderate exertion, occasional aches and pains, fatigue, etc.). Mild psychopathology. Mild functional limitations and/or mild impairment of well being. |
| 2 | Presence of established obesity-related chronic disease (e.g., hypertension, type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea, osteoarthritis, reflux disease, polycystic ovary syndrome, anxiety disorder). Moderate limitations in activities of daily living and/or well being. |
| 3 | Established end-organ damage, such as myocardial infarction, heart failure, diabetic complications, or incapacitating osteoarthritis. Significant psychopathology. Significant functional limitations and/or impairment of well being. |
| 4 | Severe (potentially end-stage) disabilities from obesity-related chronic diseases. Severe disabling psychopathology. Severe functional limitations and/or severe impairment of well being. |
